lines.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right now!
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: At least the bread is ready in the oven.
We need less than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعتمد, بيعتمد).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We rely on Nour at reception.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببنشر, بيبنشر).

examples.trans: The dairy van got a flat tyre outside town.
The tyre went flat on the road this morning.

meanings.note: Collective plural بيض ('eggs'), singulative بيضة ('one egg'), dual بيضتين ('two eggs').

examples.trans: I fried two eggs for breakfast.
Hot eggs are delicious with bread.

meanings.note: Collective تفاح ('apples'), singulative تفاحة ('an apple').

examples.trans: I bought red apples from the shop.
Apple jam is delicious at breakfast.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تلاجات.

examples.trans: The cold milk is inside the fridge.
Open the fridge and check the butter.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أجبان.

examples.trans: White cheese is tasty with mint.
We bought cheese and olives for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جوعانة, plural: جوعانين).

examples.trans: Eight hungry guests are coming down to breakfast.
Come eat, you look hungry.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I would like coffee with hot milk.
We bought three bottles of milk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Numeral 'fifty'.

examples.trans: Here is fifty dinars from the cash box.
She saved fifty piastres on the bill.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دكاكين.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I bought milk and bread from the shop.

meanings.note: Jordan's national currency (JOD), divided into 100 piastres (قرش).

examples.trans: The bill is twenty dinars, please.
I gave him fifty dinars in cash.

meanings.note: Used mainly in polite/earnest requests: أرجوك (to a man), أرجوكي (to a woman), أرجوكم (plural) — 'please!'.

examples.trans: Please write down that sentence!
Please do not open the white parcel.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركض, بيركض).

examples.text: اركضي بسرعة قبل ما يصحوا الضيوف!
examples.trans: Run fast before the guests wake up!
You ran across half the town this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زوايا.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.text: بدي خبز سخن مع شوية زبدة.
examples.trans: I would like warm bread with a little butter.
Is this salted butter or unsalted?

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سيارات.

examples.trans: We heard a car stop outside.

examples.text: ما في صوت سيارات جوا الساحة.
examples.trans: There is no sound of cars inside the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طوارئ.

examples.trans: We have a small emergency in the kitchen!
The emergency key hangs beside the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عجين.

examples.trans: The bread dough is ready in the oven.
She left the dough to rest half an hour.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فواتير.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper gave me a receipt and change.
We sorted all the invoices in the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قناني.

examples.trans: We bought three bottles of fresh milk.
Put the bottle of cold water on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قهاوي.

examples.text: بتحبي قهوة مع هيل ولا شاي؟
examples.trans: Would you like cardamom coffee or tea?
Morning coffee is ready on the stove.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كياس.

examples.trans: Give me a cloth bag for the shop.
I carried the bag of apples and bread.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألبان.

examples.trans: The dairy van arrives early in the morning.
We have yoghurt, olive oil, and thyme for breakfast.

meanings.note: Also used in the mild Jordanian exclamation يا لطيف! ('goodness gracious!').

examples.trans: Hot bread makes people pleasant!
Goodness gracious, the suitcase is so heavy!

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Plural-form noun that is THE everyday Jordanian/Levantine word for money.

examples.trans: Take cash from the box for the shop.
We saved money for annual maintenance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نقط.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'there / over there' (لهناك 'over there').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes over there.
Can you run over there and back?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.
